name: Question 29
problem: At a geological site, an object is found with $75%$ of its original chlorine-36 content. Given that the half-life of chlorine-36 is $301$ thousand years, approximately how old is the object?
worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

Since we know that ${t}_{1/2}=301$ thousand years, we have

$$
301=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}\,⇒\,k=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{301}.
$$

So, we have

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/301}.
$$

We wish to calculate the time $t$ such that $M(t)=0.75{M}_{0}.$ So, we set up our equation as follows:

$$
0.75{M}_{0}={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/301}
$$

Solving this equation for $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0.75{M}_{0} & ={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/301} \\ 0.75\cancel{{M}_{0}} & =\cancel{{M}_{0}}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/301} \\ 0.75 & ={e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/301} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.75) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/301}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.75) & =-\frac{t\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{301} \\ t & =-\frac{301\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.75)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ t & ≈125.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the object is approximately $125$ thousand years old.

html:
Question 29
?

At a geological site, an object is found with 75% of its original chlorine-36 content. Given that the half-life of chlorine-36 is 301 thousand years, approximately how old is the object?

a
143 thousand years
b
112 thousand years
c
125 thousand years
d
236 thousand years
e
92 thousand years
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The mass M(t) of a radioactive substance at time t can be modeled by the differential equation

M′(t)=−kM(t),M(0)=M0.

The general solution to this equation is

M(t)=M0e−kt.

The half-life t1/2 is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

t1/2=ln⁡2k.

Since we know that t1/2=301 thousand years, we have

301=ln⁡2k⇒k=ln⁡2301.

So, we have M(t)=M0e−tln⁡2/301.

We wish to calculate the time t such that M(t)=0.75M0. So, we set up our equation as follows:

0.75M0=M0e−tln⁡2/301

Solving this equation for t, we get

0.75M0=M0e−tln⁡2/3010.75M0=M0e−tln⁡2/3010.75=e−tln⁡2/301ln⁡(0.75)=ln⁡(e−tln⁡2/301)ln⁡(0.75)=−tln⁡2301t=−301⋅ln⁡(0.75)ln⁡2t≈125.

Therefore, we conclude that the object is approximately 125 thousand years old.
